newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly lower but Dec higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly lower but Dec higher.

text.p: December CME live cattle ended higher on commercial short covering while other months slipped to lower closes on weaker-than-expected cash cattle prices paid this week, traders said. Feeder cattle values firmed late in the session lower corn futures, to end mostly firmer.

December showed the most support, reflecting its already-large discount to current cash levels. December cattle futures closed 0.100 cent a lb higher at 65.725 cents while fed cattle traded liberally at feedlots at $71.00 per cwt.

Traders said sellers are going to have a hard time pushing December much lower, considering its discount to cash. Kill rates will climb into the winter, but demand for beef is uncertain which will make sellers nervous at current prices.

Liquidation kept October pressured with some traders citing the weaker-than-expected tone to cash markets. Although fed cattle supplies will be tight until sometime in November, falling beef prices and cash cattle sales at $71, down $2 from last week's top price, encouraged selling.
Cash beef prices declined another $0.27 to $0.85 per cwt at noon Thursday, the lowest level since September 30.
Fund selling and spillover weakness from pork pits also weighed on the market, traders said.
Refco bought December late after trading on both sides of the market early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, trading was light with bidding on the 66 supporting the premium. Volatility was steady to firm in February, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle futures much of the day but firmed late on support linked to lower corn futures. Locals bought November to support the long leg of their spreads. LIT division of First Options bought October again late and offset early selling by Prudential Securities, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.17 at $63.17 per cwt, the lowest level since September 4.

Live cattle futures finished 0.100 cent a lb higher to 0.175 lower with only December up at 65.725 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.275 higher to 0.300 lower with October up 0.175 at 63.350 and November up most at 63.950 cents.
